A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a persistent, purely functional interface and implementation of triangulated surfaces and simplicial complexes that is suitable for a wide range of problems, and for which the performance is competitive with existing, mutable implementations.
, for many applications, we can now have the best of both worlds: persistent data structures with the same performance as their mutable counterparts.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the cost of persistence is often ignored, it can be achieved with a constant factor overhead, and that this cost is often not a significant factor in end-to-end performance.
persistence is not a performance killer, but rather a performance enhancer, allowing us to use the same code base in multiple applications, including parallel ones.
